slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Parallel Postulate: through a point not on a line, there is exactly one line parallel to the given line.

We already proved there is at least one parallel (5.6). That there is only one cannot be proved from the other postulates. For about 2,000 years mathematicians tried. In the 1800s, Bolyai, Lobachevsky and Gauss developed a geometry in which it fails, and Beltrami showed in 1868 that it is consistent, so it must be assumed. Euclid's fifth postulate says the same thing in a different form.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Which part of the Parallel Postulate needs to be assumed: that a parallel exists, or that it is unique?
slides.reveal: That it is unique. Existence was already proved in 5.6 without the postulate.
